title: docs(react): declare that the render path is not a validation door (objectui#9746)
body:
Part of #9746

Letter B on objectui#9746 (director seat summon 24, maintainer agreed 2026-09-18) ruled this card **text only**: the render path stays exactly as it is and is *declared* so. No code path changes here — the dev-only structural walker is untouched.

## What landed

- `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md` — a new section, **Render is not a validation door**, placed between *Error Handling* and *TypeScript Support*. It states that `SchemaRenderer` never parses a document against the published Zod schema, that the one document check on the render path is `@object-ui/core`'s hand-written structural walker behind a development-only guard, and that a production build therefore validates nothing before it draws. It names the three doors that do validate and warns that the walker and the schema do not share an accept set.
- `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — **one comment line** beside the `__DEV__` guard in `validateSchemaOnce`, pointing at that section by heading (⛔ not by a line address — commandment 11).
- `.changeset/9746-render-path-not-a-validation-door.md` — empty front matter.

## Clause-②: no

This moves no published accept set. Tested rather than asserted, two instruments, each with a lit control:

1. **New exported symbols over the non-test diff: 0.** Instrument: `git diff -U0` excluding `__tests__` and `*.test.*`, counting added lines matching an `export` word boundary. Lit control on the same instrument: commit `3b6d53bc3c` on `packages/react/src` scores 1 on the identical grep, so a zero here is an absence and not a dead instrument.
2. **The code file's change is provably a comment.** With comments stripped and blank lines dropped, `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` is byte-identical before and after — both sides sha256 `3c5b9feb5d6142d93f0222e6c2d426efa5286aab4604690b0a5410dbdfd03387`. Lit control on the same instrument and corpus: mutating one non-comment identifier in the same file makes the same comparison differ. Nothing the build emits moves.

Documentation under `content/` sits outside every package directory, so it is in no published `files` list; lit control on that reading: 39 published packages list `dist` in `files`, zero list `content`.

## Changeset level, and why

Empty front matter — **no release**. The reading is the one above: the only edit to published source is a comment, which no build emits, and `content/` ships in no package. No runtime behaviour, export, type or manifest field moves. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` agrees in its own words: *"Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing nothing, which is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate."*

## The reading was re-taken at head before a word was written

The card's reproduction used a retired `body` key on a `chatbot` node as its probe, and `2acd8e109c` moved that instrument. Re-taken on `origin/main` `f156329bb5`:

1. **Does `SchemaRenderer` still skip the Zod root parse at render, with the walker behind `__DEV__`?** Yes. Comment-stripped, `SchemaRenderer.tsx` scores 0 for `zod` and 0 for `safeValidateSchema`; lit control on the same instrument, `packages/react/src/spec-input.ts` scores 1. The only validator call site in `packages/react/src` outside tests is `validateSchema` from `@object-ui/core`, reached through `validateSchemaOnce`, which returns early when the `NODE_ENV` guard is false.
2. **Does anything validate on the render path in a production build?** No. The guard is false, `validateSchemaOnce` returns `{ valid: true }` before it reads anything, and the `data-obj-schema-invalid` attribute is gated on the same flag.
3. **Are the two doors real at head?** Yes. `content/docs/guide/metadata-diagnostics.md` opens by stating that every metadata item a package ships is validated against its Zod schema when the framework loads it, and describes the `_diagnostics` envelope Studio surfaces. On the authoring side, `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts` and `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` both import and run `safeValidateSchema` from `@object-ui/types/zod`.

**Behavioural probe, both readers over one corpus** (run through `tsx` against the source, ⛔ no file left behind):

| document | `@object-ui/core` `validateSchema` (the render path) | `safeValidateSchema` (the Zod door) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `chatbot` + retired key holding a node | ACCEPT | REFUSE — the retirement's own message |
| `chatbot` + retired key holding an array of nodes | ACCEPT | REFUSE — same |
| `chatbot` + retired key holding a string | ACCEPT | REFUSE — same |
| `chatbot` + retired key holding a number | ACCEPT | REFUSE — same |
| `chatbot` + retired key holding a record | ACCEPT | REFUSE — same |
| same node nested one level under a `page` | ACCEPT | not probed |

Firing controls on the walker fire: `null` gives `INVALID_SCHEMA schema: Schema must be an object`, a typeless child gives `MISSING_REQUIRED schema.children[0].type: type is required`, a retired node-type spelling gives `RETIRED_TYPE`. Absent control clean: a well-formed `chatbot` with no retired key is accepted by both readers. So both instruments are lit and both zeros are real.

⚠️ **One of the card's own readings no longer reproduces, and the prose does not assert it.** The card records a refinement — that a *record*-shaped value IS refused by the render path, but for the unrelated reason that the walker descends the key as a children channel and reports a missing `type`. At head the walker reads `children` only: objectui#6771 retired the second spelling inside this very walker, and the comment-stripped validator scores 0 for that key name against a control of 7 for `children` in the same file. The record shape is now simply ACCEPTED, as the table shows. The section therefore makes the general, measured statement — the two readers do not share an accept set, in either direction — and ⛔ does not describe an accidental coverage that no longer exists. That is the sentence class PR objectui#9360 was rejected for, and it was the point of re-taking the reading.
